habit: After each card window: run the open microbenchmarks below that fit the window (each is a loop body for the tests/bench/knc-char catalog: 32 units per round, 1/2/4 threads, about one second each).
Import each result with import-native; a value enters a profile only as a new profile version, with the row named as a calibration row.

Add the window's compiled runs as held-out cases: the binary or object, the input the run used (dumped arrays as init.memory file blocks), the log, measurement.json. Record the prediction (validate_heldout.py --cases --record) before reading the measured numbers.
Rerun validate_heldout.py; the decision bar and the open-miss table in references/validation.md are regenerated from it. A row that changes a rule moves to calibration and stops counting as held out.

decision_bar.note: on held-out compiled loops only; reported by validate_heldout.py as 'decision_bar'

microbenchmarks.settles: cost of the publication fence and of locked read-modify-write instructions
microbenchmarks.variants: throughput at 1/2/4 threads; a second row with 'lock addq %r8, 0(%rsi)' on a private line
microbenchmarks.why: every region with a lock prefix stops with missing_parameter today

microbenchmarks.settles: the exact bit patterns of vrcp23ps and vrsqrt23ps (the twin substitutes the correctly rounded value and marks results approximate)
microbenchmarks.variants: a capture program, not a timing row: for every significand (2^23 inputs in [1,2) for vrcp23ps; 2^24 for vrsqrt23ps, both exponent parities) dump the result's 32 bits; 32 MB plus 64 MB of output, one core, under a minute. The twin then loads the tables (fixtures/tables/) and both instructions become exact; dependence on the exponent is checked on a 256-exponent sample
microbenchmarks.why: PhiWeather's vectorized exp/log/pow/divide/sqrt sequences depend on these bits; without the table every such loop is marked approximate

microbenchmarks.settles: result latency and pairing of vgetexpps, vgetmantps, vscaleps, vgmaxps, vgminps, vpblendmd, vpcmpd, vfixupnanps and stmxcsr
microbenchmarks.variants: .lat and .rt rows for each mnemonic (the characterization catalog form), plus 'stmxcsr 0(%rsi); movl 0(%rsi), %eax' as a chain
microbenchmarks.why: the twin charges every one of them the measured 4-cycle vector latency (vector_arith) or 6 (vector_long for vrcp23ps); none is measured; stmxcsr is charged as a scalar store

microbenchmarks.settles: scatter cost per cache line and per execution
microbenchmarks.variants: indices on one line and on sixteen lines, .rt, at 1/2/4 threads (the gather_all / gather_scattered pair for scatters)
microbenchmarks.why: every region with a scatter stops with missing_parameter today
microbenchmarks.owner_request: PhiWeather, 2026-11-16, after M4: 413 scatters in the 13 WRF hot routines stop the timing

microbenchmarks.why: the profile holds a Pentium prior (46 cycles) charged to both widths

microbenchmarks.settles: fsqrt latency and whether it serializes the x87 unit
microbenchmarks.variants: .lat (fsqrt on the running value) and .rt, 1/2/4 threads
microbenchmarks.why: the profile holds a Pentium prior (70 cycles)

microbenchmarks.settles: fldcw, fnstcw and fnstsw cost (float-to-integer conversion sequences use them)
microbenchmarks.variants: each instruction alone as well; 'fnstsw %ax' after fucom
microbenchmarks.why: the profile holds a Pentium prior (7 cycles for all three)

microbenchmarks.settles: the split of the 7 cycles measured for 'fldl m; fmull m' and the half cycle the row loop is over-predicted by
microbenchmarks.variants: (a) fldl; fstp  (b) fldl; fmull 8(%rsi); fstp  (c) fldl; faddl 8(%rsi); fstp  (d) the S12-31 row loop with 1, 2, 3 and 4 products per row, to separate the per-iteration and the per-row cost
microbenchmarks.why: the S12-31 and S12-30 loops are predicted 3% slow uniformly; only the sum of the two latencies is measured

microbenchmarks.settles: whether any scalar instruction pairs with an x87 instruction (S12-31 measured the jump only)
microbenchmarks.variants: x87 followed by add, by mov, by a load, by a store; compared with the two instructions alone
microbenchmarks.why: the rule 'x87 issues alone' is applied to every scalar partner

microbenchmarks.settles: how long after a store a load may issue, same line and other line, vector and scalar
microbenchmarks.variants: aliasing and non-aliasing pairs with 0 to 4 nops between store and load; the same with movq stores and loads; 1/2/4 threads
microbenchmarks.why: spill_reload.rt at one thread (5.09 measured, 4.0 predicted) and the two-thread C9 memory chains (12.0, 11.0 measured, 8 to 9 predicted) are open; the scalar rule is assumed

microbenchmarks.settles: movslq and movzbl cost and pairing
microbenchmarks.variants: .lat through the address and through the value; paired with a preceding add
microbenchmarks.why: every sparse and indexed loop starts with one; both values are assumed

microbenchmarks.settles: the core cycle lost after a taken branch at two threads, and for jknzd
microbenchmarks.variants: c10.branch.fixed at two threads (only one and four were measured); a loop of taken jknzd

microbenchmarks.settles: gather cost between one line and sixteen lines, and at two and four threads
microbenchmarks.why: only the two endpoints were measured; the one-line-per-execution rule interpolates

microbenchmarks.settles: L2 hardware prefetcher depth and stride limit, and the memory service rate at one to four threads
microbenchmarks.variants: memory-sized buffer read with strides of 1, 2, 3 and 4 lines; 2 to 16 interleaved streams; with 2 MiB pages
microbenchmarks.why: depth 16 is fitted to one row; the four-thread stream rows are 7 to 10% high

microbenchmarks.settles: L1 replacement under set pressure (the model uses true LRU)
microbenchmarks.variants: 9, 10 and 12 lines of one L1 set read round-robin and in a random order
microbenchmarks.why: the S12-30 small cases are predicted 14 to 18% slow, most of it L1 conflict misses of the random column accesses

open_misses.suspected: L1 conflict misses under true LRU, and the random input instance (seed spread 2.5 to 6%)

open_misses.row: S12-31 row loops and HPCG kernels

open_misses.suspected: store-to-load interlock is one cycle longer at one thread
store and load contention between two threads
occupancy.scatter_cycles_per_line unmeasured; vrcp23ps/vrsqrt23ps bit patterns unknown (results approximate); jump tables in advect_scalar/advect_scalar_pd not followed by the binary adapter

held_out_additions: M4 corpus: for each of the 17 programs, the two or three hottest functions named by its qualified profile, from the installed binaries (scripts/from_binary.py), with the fixed-work input's arrays dumped once, and the function's exclusive time from the same profile run. Target: 50 compiled loops or more.

PhiWeather WRF: the 13 hot routines of the patched build (tests/heldout_native/wrf_coverage.py lists object and symbol) with one timestep's arrays dumped per routine and the routine's time share from the run profile.

PhiWeather WRF: the hot advection and microphysics routines from the card build (objects or wrf.exe), with each routine's share of a timed step from the existing run profiles (rollup manifest), and per-routine times where the profile has them.
PhiChat: the GEMV and decode loops with one prompt's tensors dumped.
Each S12/S13 A/B window: the before and after functions of the ticket as a two-variant case.

other_cards.card-3120-documented: no 3120 measurement exists in the project; '--profile 3100' runs are the 7120 card with fewer threads and less memory. On a real 3120: the characterization catalog (tests/bench/knc-char, about ten minutes) gives memory latency, the memory service rate and the sustained bandwidths; core timing is expected to match the 7120 layer and the same run checks that.
other_cards.card-5110p-literature: as for the 3120; the L2 and memory latencies in the profile are literature values from other samples.
